title: Mahdids
capsule: The Mahdids were a short-lived Yemeni dynasty founded by the religious agitator Ali bin Mahdi, who built a power base in the Tihama lowlands by undermining the Najahid rulers of Zabid before his death in 1159. His son Mahdi bin Ali (d. 1163) and grandson Abd an-Nabi extended control over much of coastal and central Yemen, including Ta'izz and Ibb, ruling with strict religious severity—wine drinking was a capital offense. The Ayyubid prince Turan Shah, dispatched by Saladin, conquered Zabid on 13 May 1174, capturing Abd an-Nabi; the dynasty ended when Abd an-Nabi was executed in 1176.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Mahdid territorial extent is poorly documented; their control was largely a matter of regional submission rather than administered boundaries, and the geometric attestation window of 1169–1507 in this dataset appears to reflect Wikidata date choices that differ from the dynasty's historical endpoint of 1174.
